title: Write a GLSL TOP
summary: Official Derivative guide for GLSL TOP image shaders, covering GLSL 4.60 pixel and compute outputs, dimensional sampler arrays, non-uniform sampler access, POP buffers, texture info uniforms, 3D/array outputs, atomic counters, specialization constants, multi-color-buffer output, vertex-shader caveats, and Vulkan-era GLSL gotchas.
guidance: Use this article when a plan needs GLSL TOP shader source, input TOP sampling, compute-output helpers, multi-buffer output, or POP buffer reads from a TOP shader.
Pixel shaders should write declared output variables such as layout(location = 0) out vec4 and pass color through TDOutputSwizzle.
Compute shaders should use TDImageStoreOutput and TDImageLoadOutput for output textures; TDOutputSwizzle is handled internally by those helpers.

For input TOPs, use the sTD*Inputs sampler arrays and TDTexInfo metadata rather than hand-declared samplers; sampler arrays are split by dimensionality and recompiled around TD_NUM_2D_INPUTS, TD_NUM_3D_INPUTS, TD_NUM_2D_ARRAY_INPUTS, and TD_NUM_CUBE_INPUTS.

Wrap dynamic sampler or image-output array indices in nonuniformEXT() when the index is decided during shader execution, such as by UV-dependent branching, because sampler access is otherwise expected to be dynamically uniform.
Use sTDNoiseMap and sTDSineLookup for the built-in random and sine lookup samplers when those lightweight lookup textures are enough.

For POP attribute buffers, pair TDBuffer_AttribName(elementIndex, arrayIndex) with TDBufferLength_AttribName() and cTDBufferArraySize_AttribName so buffer indexing and array-size assumptions are explicit.
Use uTD2DInfos, uTD3DInfos, uTD2DArrayInfos, uTDCubeInfos, and uTDOutputInfo for input/output resolution and depth metadata instead of hand-maintained width, height, or depth uniforms.
Use uTDCurrentDepth when writing 3D Texture or 2D Texture Array outputs, and use uTDPass when Num Passes on the GLSL TOP Common page controls pass-specific shader behavior.

For Atomic Counters, declare atomic_uint values without online-example layout binding prefixes when TouchDesigner can assign bindings, and use atomicCounterIncrement() only for shared counter-style state.
Use Specialization Constants with layout(constant_id = 0) for rarely changing shader modes; they cache specialized variants and should not be used for constantly changing values.
When sampling neighboring pixels, multiple texture() calls can use offsets derived from uTD2DInfos, while textureOffset() is suitable only for limited nearby offsets.

For # of Color Buffers, pixel shaders must write every declared output in all cases; use Render Select TOP to inspect buffers beyond the first, and do not rely on undefined unwritten values preserving previous frames.

For compute shaders with multiple color buffers, remember sTDComputeOutputs[] is sized to the configured output buffer count even though TDImageStoreOutput()/TDImageLoadOutput() are the preferred current helpers for output texture access.

If you provide a custom vertex shader, vUV is not automatically available in the pixel shader; pass your own uv[0]-derived coordinate through and keep gl_Position on the TOP-aligned quad with TDSOPToProj(P).
Do not include a #version line in shader DATs because TouchDesigner inserts it.
